requested_part_assessment.actual_requested_clause: May the two players interleave Gather and Damage?

fact_assessments.expected: One player must finish the full Gather-and-Damage instruction sequence before the next starts; the proposed interleaving is not allowed.
fact_assessments.observed: Each player resolves all their own instructions first, then the next player resolves theirs. So A Gathers and deals Damage before B Gathers and deals Damage; players do not interleave all Gathers before all Damage.

summary_support.quote: For “each player,” one player follows all instructions, then the next;

grades.reason: Both Gather and Damage must finish for one player before the next starts; the proposed interleaving is rejected. Player-order selection is contextual key background, not an additional required fact.

requested_part_assessment.actual_requested_clause: Cleanup or outcome check first?

fact_assessments.expected: Correct the illegal position after the completed action tree but before checking victory/defeat; check the cleaned-up state.
fact_assessments.observed: Correct illegal placement before checking outcomes. Cleanup happens after the action and all triggered actions, and before the outcome check.

summary_support.quote: **After the primary action and all triggered actions finish**, remaining illegal humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land. grades.reason: The answer places cleanup after the completed action tree and before the outcome check. Nearest-land destination and non-action status are contextual background for this ordering question.

requested_part_assessment.actual_requested_clause: When the Fast threshold is applied

summary_support.quote: Apply a threshold changing Speed, Range or targeting when checking that attribute, before the ordinary effects: for example, Thunderspeaker's met Fast threshold permits using its Innate in Fast.

grades.reason: The met Speed modifier applies at the phase/Speed check before ordinary effects, permitting Fast use. The stipulated game-state threshold need not be separately repeated.
